subject: Integration kickoff: SDK quicklaunch, local sandbox & sample apps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai

Subject: Integration kickoff: SDK quicklaunch, local sandbox & sample apps

Hi Daniel — great call today, thanks for the context. Quick recap and proposed quicklaunch plan so engineering can start picking up work: 

Summary of BrightBridge goals
- Customer-facing QA assistant and document search for technical support docs (high recall + low-latency snippets)
- Reranking for search results and a lightweight tool-calling flow to fetch account metadata from their internal CRM
- PoC constraints: 3 model routes (generation, embedding, reranker), latency target ~ <150ms tail for generation on short prompts, dataset contains PII (so private deployment consideration later)

Proposed quicklaunch steps (90–120m effort to get running locally + examples)
1) Environment & SDKs
   - Python: 3.10+ (venv), redwood-sdk-python pinned to v0.9.x for PoC samples
   - TypeScript: Node 18+, TS 5.x, redwood-js-sdk sample for tool-calls
   - Docker: use docker-compose.local.yml to run: local mockserver (api proxy), sample app, and a mini vector store (FAISS via python container)

2) Auth & secrets (PoC vs production)
   - PoC: API key stored in .env for local runs (we'll provide scripted env loader)
   - Production: OIDC + customer KMS; we'll prepare notes for key rotation and RBAC

3) Routing & model variants
   - Route by intent: /search -> embedding + reranker, /chat -> generation model
   - Canary policy: 80/20 prod fallback; SDK supports route weights and model fallback to a quantized variant if capacity is constrained

4) Structured output & tool calling
   - Enable tool_calling flag in SDK; sample flow: user question -> generator suggests a tool call -> call internal CRM microservice -> structured JSON back into generator for final answer
   - We'll include a TypeScript sample with a tool adapter that demonstrates the call/response pattern

5) Embeddings & reranker flow
   - Local PoC: embed documents, index with FAISS, run nearest-neighbor then pass top-k to reranker model for final ordering
   - We'll include embedding dimension and example hyperparams in playbook attachment

Local testing checklist (attached docker-compose and sample apps)
- Start mockserver and FAISS container
- Run python samplebot: python samplebot/run_local.py --env .env.local
- Run ts-searcher: npm install && npm run dev (uses SDK sample for tool-calls)
- Smoke test prompts included in eval_prompt_set.csv

Attachments included: redwood_quicklaunch_playbook.pdf, brightbridge_sample_apps_v1.zip, docker-compose.local.yml, eval_prompt_set.csv

Asks / next steps
- Daniel: confirm PoC scope (models & latency target) and whether we can use PoC API key flow
- Internal: can engineering provision a dev sandbox (containers + ephemeral FAISS) and review the playbook before the technical sync?
- Propose technical sync: Tues Feb 28 9:30am PT — confirm availability

Thanks — I will follow up with a single-thread checklist for engineers after we lock the sync slot.

—
Marissa Cole

Marissa — appreciate the write-up, looks comprehensive. A few clarifications from our side:
- PoC: yes to API key flow for initial work. Production will need OIDC/KMS but that can come later.
- Model slate: generation (chatty assistant), embeddings (search), reranker (smaller LM) — we want to test 1 larger open model and 1 quantized variant for cost comparison.
- Latency: target for short prompts <150ms tail (95th). If quantized variant can get us to a 2x cost advantage and keeps p95 <200ms, that’d be acceptable.
- Reranker example: can you include a minimal reranker that takes top-10, runs pairwise scoring and returns re-ordered ids? That exact pattern is what our search infra expects.

Thanks — sketched a short tech note below after a quick pass on the playbook. High-level architecture notes and PoC recommendations: 

1) Local composition
   - docker-compose.local.yml with 4 services: mock-proxy (routes to redwood-hosted API or local mock), python-samplebot, ts-searcher, faiss-indexer (python). Use a separate container for a lightweight redis to simulate KV cache.

2) Model routing & cost
   - Use route-level model_aliases: {chat: gptx-1, chat-quant: gptx-1-q4} and specify in SDK config a fallback list [gptx-1, gptx-1-q4]. SDK will attempt primary then fallback on capacity errors.
   - Batching: set continuous_batching.window_ms=10 for local PoC to emulate production batching behavior while keeping latency low.

3) Structured output / tool-calling pattern
   - Generator prompt includes a schema template. Example (pseudocode):
     system: you are a JSON-only assistant that can call tools.
     user: ...
     model: when tool suggested -> emit {"tool": "crm_lookup", "args": {"account_id": "..."}}
   - The TS sample will include a tool adapter that accepts that JSON and issues an HTTP call to mock-proxy, then injects the JSON response back to the model via the SDK's tool_return API.

4) Embeddings & rerank
   - Use embed dim 1536 (match model), run ANN via FAISS (IVF+PQ) for quick PoC. Top-K=10 -> reranker model does pairwise scoring over candidates. Reranker should be smaller to keep cost down (e.g., rerank-compact)

5) Test harness & evals
   - Use eval_prompt_set.csv for smoke checks; include a small script run_evals.sh that runs the pipeline end-to-end and records latency + quality metrics. Save outputs to /artifacts for review.

Potential blockers: if BrightBridge insists on private deployment for PoC due to PII, we'll need a short onboarding for their infra team (VPC peering or on-prem package). For now PoC via hosted API + API key is fine.

I will drop a short diagram and a sample docker-compose snippet into the drive link and update the playbook.

—Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Platforms
